catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a start command with no input: cap.actuation.pump.v1 requires flow_rate and direction in uL/s, which would need a tubing calibration the clone does not state; the upstream class has only the native start command 1H.

No catalogue stop class fits this pump controller: the upstream stop is the 1I command with no acknowledgement and no input, while cap.actuation.pump.v1 is a run/flow capability, not a stop; the safe-state action is kept as an extension with an inline output schema.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names PythonObjectDriver, but the upstream Ismatec methods queue a request and return immediately; only the worker thread's callback carries the reply (src/instruments/ismatec/ismatec.py:44-60, 62-84), so this package is a direct decorated Driver over the entry symbol instruments.ismatec.ismatec:Ismatec. The card lists Ika and Bronkhorst too; Ika has no _process_request, so its queued commands never reach the line (src/instruments/ika/ika.py:41-69 against src/instruments/instrument.py:42-48), and Bronkhorst calls super().__init__(port) on object and has no _queue (src/instruments/bronkhorst/bronkhorst.py:19-27). Only Ismatec was driven. The card's catalogue candidates do not bind this device: cap.actuation.pump.v1 declares flow_rate in uL/s, while the clone's set_flowrate and get_flowrate docstrings state pump rpm (1/min) and the clone gives no tubing calibration; cap.fluid.dispense.v1 requires a labware/well target and a pipette volume, neither of which the class has. The setpoint write is served by cap.device.configure.v1; the start and stop actions are extension ids with inline schemas and the catalogue_requests below. The setpoint range is Limit.operator_required because no text of the clone states a pump speed range; site-limits.example.json is an example only (0..100 /min) and every write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until an operator overlay supplies the range of the real unit. The fake is an in-memory analytic stand-in, not a recording: it calls callbacks synchronously, has no 0.3 s worker timing, and models a stop as immediate. The real upstream serializes start/set/get/stop on one queue, so a stop waits behind already queued requests, and the class reads no stop acknowledgement and has no run-state query; the start and stop actions report the command they queued, not sensed motion or quiescence. The hardware backend (native.py) was never run: it needs the upstream instruments package importable (the clone's src on PYTHONPATH) and pyserial, neither of which the card's install block declares, and this model-authored R2 package is refused by the loader until a human sets reviewed_by. Only the fake backend was checked; no ROS or [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct Driver over instruments.ismatec.ismatec:Ismatec line by line against ismatec.py, instrument.py and the rest of the clone at the pin, native.py included, with the gate and collect.py --strict re-run (the author's pass reproduced, digest sha256:2b5eecc43b70bcd60df1eba3f84f2d9d3171c5aa912b52fc52a44783ee5772a2). The pass rested on the queued native stop 1I, bound as the @estop and as the safe_state=True action stop_pump, both returning at once: the upstream reads no reply to 1I and has no run-state query (ismatec.py:44-60, 20-90), a stop waits behind every queued request, and _process_queue has no exception handler (instrument.py:42-48), so one 1S reply that float() cannot parse (an empty read after timeout=0.5 included; the runtime reads rate before and after every command) ends the single worker and no later request, the stop included, is ever written, yet the SDK reported every e-stop completed with the safe state achieved (review/lists/hw2-dayr3n33-probe_dead_worker.py: completed while 1I was never written); under the user's decision of 2026-11-04 this actuator stays blocked. The reviewer made the @estop queue 1I and then raise SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held, made stop_pump an ordinary action that waits for the upstream callback, renamed the start and stop outputs to written (the callback confirms only a port write), rewrote safe_state and the docstring, added a finiteness check on the rate read, and rewrote seven facts that said more than their lines (a 'receives', a queue and a thread cited off their lines, a pyserial timeout unit, 'before any pump command', a universal surface claim) and added nine (queue, worker, imports, install, the clone's deployment) in driver.py and facts.md; fake.py now models the worker ending on an exception and no longer zeroes the speed on a stop; test_driver.py replaces two doubles with behaviour the upstream does not have (a non-numeric callback value, a stop() that raises) by cases for the unconfirmed e-stop, the dead worker and a non-finite reply; native.py's docstring no longer claims a lib.helper_functions import, an installable package or that Ismatec(port) opens the port (its code is unchanged); reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json were regenerated. The gate now fails only G3 SAFE-045 (R2 hardware with neither an independent stop nor a safe-state action), the expected blocked state (stable digest sha256:fc07f4c387b77d03eb85646223aa0e48d21a526929bd27760c2b6526c5b55926; G5, G6, G8 and G9 not run; the seven package cases pass and the stock test_gate fails while blocked), and the author's notes and catalogue_requests reason that call stop_pump the safe-state action are superseded. For the human reviewer: An Ismatec peristaltic pump over a serial line (R2: a dispensing pump). The only stop is 1I, written by the upstream's single queue worker with no reply read and no run-state query, so nothing confirms that the pump stopped, and the clone documents no independent physical stop. Any exception in a request (a 1S reply float() cannot parse, such as an empty read after timeout=0.5 or a lone '*', or a serial write error) ends that worker silently: every later request, the stop included, is dropped while the upstream methods still return normally, and the runtime reads rate (1S) before and after every command. The e-stop therefore always reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED and the background retry re-queues 1I until an operator reset (a reset touches nothing on the device; a new start is required). Opening the hardware backend writes '@1' and '1M' (their effect is not in the clone) and starts the worker; the class has no close method. The set point is int()-truncated and zero-padded to at least five digits with no upper refusal, and its rpm unit rests only on docstrings: check the 1S encoding and what the pump answers to 1S against the manual before choosing the operator range (the example overlay 0..100 is a placeholder). The clone's docker-compose service (restart unless-stopped) opens the same /dev/ttyUSB0 at import and starts or stops the pump on DeltaV OPC UA node changes: never run it beside this endpoint. Unblocking needs the pump's status or acknowledgement reply from a cited manual or pinned companion source, read by a stop path that does not depend on the shared worker. Broken at the pin, for whoever unblocks it: Ika has no _process_request, Bronkhorst cannot be constructed, ismatec_asynchronous.py never imports Serial and ismatec_queue.py has no _process_request; ismatec_synchronous.py writes 1I directly but reads no reply either.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Adversarial verification of the claude-opus-5-5 review (block) by a different model (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): the verifier agreed and found no blocker or major. The block is genuine and I found no blocker or major. I re-ran `mhs.driver check`, which fails only G3 (SAFE-045: R2 hardware with neither an independent stop nor a safe-state action). G5, G6, G8 and G9 are skipped. I also re-ran `collect.py --strict`, which reports FAIL G3 with RESULT_UNTRUSTED because RESULT.json still says pass; that matches the reviewer's account. I read the upstream clone at the pin and confirmed the reviewer's key claims. `stop()` only queues a "stop" request, and the worker writes `1I` with no reply read (`ismatec.py:48-49, 58-59, 67-70`). `_process_queue` has no exception handler (`instrument.py:42-48`). `get_flowrate` runs `float()` on the reply (`ismatec.py:57`), so one unparsable reply ends the single worker and drops the stop. I found no run-state query.
